philosophy: Fail closed on everything that can be observed in CI. A gate that cannot be satisfied is not a gate, so the two requirements that need hardware or an impossible measurement are stated as what they actually are - a recorded floor to hold, and a claim to prove - rather than as a number no run can produce.

guards: coveredCount: a fall means a test was removed or weakened
percent: a fall means production code was added without a test
coverage.whyNotEnforced: WA X is an Xposed module. Its largest classes resolve obfuscated members of WhatsApp's own classes through Xposed reflection and run inside a hooked Android process, so they are exercised by a device rather than by a JVM test. Unobfuscator.kt alone is 11801 instructions at 0%; 1463 classes have zero unit coverage, and 1215 of those are the hook installation layer. A suite that covered them would have to reimplement WhatsApp. The floors are the measured state and they only go up.
coverage.bootstrap: A suite with no recorded floor records its measurement and reports instead of failing, so the first run of a new suite is never blocked on a threshold nobody has chosen. It becomes binding the moment --update pins it.

latestCompatibility.rule: Device-lab evidence is required for every target the compatibility matrix claims supported or degraded for, and for no other. A claim with no evidence, evidence from another commit, evidence older than maxEvidenceAgeDays, or evidence taken off the newest declared train is a failure.
latestCompatibility.whyNotEnforcedUnconditionally: No CI runner has a rooted LSPosed device with both WhatsApp builds installed, so demanding one unconditionally blocks every release on hardware nobody has - while proving nothing, because every cell of the matrix is `unknown`, which its own statusVocabulary defines as the only status permitted without evidence. The claim discipline that evidence was standing in for is enforced where it can be: tools/compatibility/validate_compatibility.py refuses a supported cell without resolver evidence and a verifiedAt timestamp, and its self-test proves both directions.

codeQuality.enforcedBy: the Gradle build: lintDebug, detekt, spotlessCheck

lintBaseline.why: Long vector path data in artwork this project ships unchanged. Four entries, declared explicitly because the Android Gradle Plugin does not discover lint-baseline.xml on its own - left implicit the file was inert while check_baseline.py counted it as authoritative. Every other lint finding is fixed, not baselined.

codeQuality.detektThresholds: config/detekt/detekt.yml - each limit is the measured maximum in the tree, with the file that sets it named. No baseline; the next violation fails.
